name: 通人の酒席 ふくべ
cuisine: A 1939 sake tavern two minutes behind Tokyo Station — about 41 regional sake plus Kikumasamune cask sake drawn and warmed to order, with kusaya (¥950), shime-saba (¥780), tarako (¥850) and oden (¥830) as the standing snacks; roughly ¥4,000–5,000 a head, cash only
neighborhood: Yaesu 1-chōme — 2 min from Nihombashi Station exit A7 (Ginza / Tozai / Toei Asakusa lines), 5 min from the Yaesu exit of Tokyo Station
hours_raw: 月・火・水・木・金 16:30 - 22:30／定休日：土曜日、日曜日、祝日／支払いは現金のみ
gf_detail: No gluten-free claim of any kind, and no allergen information is published. The board does hold dishes that are naturally wheat-free if you skip the soy sauce — sashimi (maguro ¥1,050, tako ¥950, ika ¥900, the 3-item moriawase ¥1,500), shime-saba, tarako, salted rakkyō ¥500, chilled tomato ¥660, wakame ¥500, hiyayakko ¥500 — and the sake itself is gluten-free. Against that: the seasoning base is ordinary wheat shōyu throughout; oden and the fried/steamed fish cakes on the same menu (はんぺん焼き ¥650, さつま揚げ ¥600, 板わさ ¥650) are wheat-bound surimi simmered in a soy broth; kinpira and the tsukemono will carry shōyu. This is a cash-only, Japanese-language counter with no allergen programme, so a celiac needs to arrive with a written card and order narrowly.
vegan_detail: Fish is the point of the place — the menu is dominated by kusaya, dried aji, sashimi, tarako, squid and tuna. What a vegan could actually eat is the edge of the board: 冷奴 (cold tofu) ¥500, 生揚げ ¥680, 塩らっきょう ¥500, 冷やしトマト ¥660, わかめ ¥500, お新香 ¥550, きんぴら ¥450 and plain 納豆 ¥440 — but the kinpira and pickles are very likely seasoned with wheat shōyu and possibly dashi, and none of this is published. Enough to drink alongside, not a meal.

chef_bio.origin: Yaesu, Chūō-ku — the shop has stood on this spot since it opened
chef_bio.background: Fukube opened in Yaesu in 1939 (Tabelog's own PR copy says 創業昭和13年, i.e. 1938; the drinks writer Nayu Shiomi and the shop's own account both give 昭和14年/1939 — the two dates coexist in the sources). It has spent its whole life as the drinking room for the station district: workers and students far from home first, then salarymen, then tourists. The second-generation owner Masao Kitajima describes the intent plainly — 'you can't linger long in a place like this, but drop in, drink pleasantly, and take some energy into tomorrow.' The sake list runs to 41 labels from around the country, anchored by Kikumasamune served from a cedar cask; the food is deliberately unfashionable — kusaya, shime-saba, oden. On 28 January 2022 the shop took down its noren and the 1964 building was demolished; it reopened on 19 December 2022 in a new building that reproduces the old frontage, the dividing walls and the Kikumasamune cask, and regulars filled it from 17:00 the next day. Tabelog selected it for 居酒屋百名店 2021.
chef_bio.philosophy: 通人の酒席 — the connoisseur's drinking seat. Nothing contrived; upright posture, an individual tray, a tokkuri and a choko.
chef_bio.specialty: Kikumasamune cask sake served warm; kusaya; shime-saba; tarako; oden; salted rakkyō.

anecdotes.text: The rebuild is the reason the room looks new: the old 1964 building came down on 28 January 2022 and the shop reopened on 19 December 2022 with the dividing walls and the Kikumasamune cask reproduced from the original.

Tabelog reviewers who knew it before the rebuild note the atmosphere is 'not quite what it was' but that the cask sake warmed to nurukan is unchanged; several mention the old shaven-headed, hachimaki-wearing counterman.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Tabelog carries the address 東京都中央区八重洲1-4-5, phone 03-3271-6065, hours 月〜金 16:30–22:30 with Sat/Sun/holidays closed, 30 seats over three floors (15-seat ground-floor counter, 18 upstairs, 12 on the third), cash only, オープン日 1939年, the 居酒屋百名店 2021 selection and the full priced food menu. Syupo (Nayu Shiomi) documents the demolition and the 19 December 2022 reopening. San-tatsu gives the same address and 16:30–22:30 hours. Hitosara and Hot Pepper carry matching listings.

gf_cross_contamination.text: A small izakaya counter with a shared kitchen turning out oden, fried fish cakes and grilled fish. No wheat-free handling is claimed anywhere.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Ordinary wheat shōyu is assumed throughout — no tamari is mentioned. The oden broth, the kinpira and the pickles all sit on it.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Fish-led menu (kusaya, dried aji, sashimi, tarako, surimi) prepared on the same counter; dashi is likely in the pickles and simmered dishes.

positives.text: The sashimi list is long and priced individually, so a naturally wheat-free order (fish plus salted rakkyō plus sake, no soy sauce) is straightforward to assemble if you can explain it.

cultural_comfort.note: An old-school Tokyo sake room, not a tourist stop: cash only, no English listed, and the etiquette is to sit up straight, order a couple of things and not camp. It is easy to reach — three minutes from the Shinkansen gates — and the noren goes out early at 16:30, which suits a pre-train drink. Thirty seats over three floors; the third floor is a single 5–12 person private banquet room on a course, and the second floor can be booked out from 20. Children are allowed. Bring a written Japanese allergy card if wheat matters; asking in English at a busy counter will not get you a reliable answer.

enrich_note: CONFIRMED. Nationwide Yahoo Japan search on 「ふくべ 八重洲 居酒屋 日本酒」 returned the Tabelog, Hitosara, Hot Pepper, Retty and San-tatsu listings all agreeing on 東京都中央区八重洲1-4-5 / 03-3271-6065. Coordinates taken from Tabelog's own embedded geodata (35.6825690887168 / 139.77154865439437), which moves the pin ~130 m from the neighbourhood centroid. Name expanded to the shop's full trading name 通人の酒席 ふくべ; 「ふくべ」 alone was correct, just short.

name: 京橋 天冨良と鮨 いしい
address_ja: 〒104-0031 東京都中央区京橋1-6-12 京橋イーサスビル B1F
cuisine: Basement counter in Kyōbashi doing a single omakase kaiseki that alternates fried-to-order tempura with Edomae nigiri — 13 to 18 courses from ¥7,800 (蝶尾) through ¥9,800 (江戸錦) and ¥12,000 (和唐内) to ¥15,000 (蘭鋳); lunch kaiseki ¥4,500–9,000, 10% service charge
neighborhood: Kyōbashi 1-chōme, in the basement of the Kyōbashi E-SUS building — 3 min from Kyōbashi Station (Ginza line), 3 min from Takaracho (Toei Asakusa line), 4–5 min from Tokyo Station Yaesu exit 5
gf_detail: Not workable. The house has one thing on the board — an omakase course — and half of it is tempura, i.e. wheat batter fried in the shared oil in front of you; the nigiri half sits on wheat soy sauce (nikiri) and the courses open with a wan and a nimono seasoned the same way. There is no gluten-free claim, no allergen page and no à la carte to retreat to. Nothing published suggests the kitchen can run a wheat-free version.
vegan_detail: A sushi-and-tempura omakase: sashimi, grilled fish, nigiri, dashi-based wan. No vegetarian or vegan course is offered and there is no à la carte. Dashi is assumed to be bonito throughout.

roles: 店主／大将 (owner-chef, unnamed in published sources)
chef_bio.background: The shop opened in November 2023 in the basement of the E-SUS building a few doors from Meidi-ya in Kyōbashi, and its own copy identifies the owner only by pedigree: a chef who trained as a sushi craftsman at a well-known house and 'sharpened his skills at a long-established, famous ryōtei' (老舗有名料亭で研鑽を積んだ職人), described elsewhere as 老舗日本料理店出身の大将. No personal name appears on the official site, on Gurunavi, on Ikyu or on Tabelog. The kitchen's stated approach is 走り・旬・名残 — the run-up, the peak and the tail of each ingredient's season — assembled daily into a single omakase running from sakizuke and wan through grilled courses to nigiri, with the tempura fried at the counter. It is 24 seats: a 6-seat counter plus 18 at tables, including a genuinely enclosed 2–6 person private room aimed at business entertaining.
chef_bio.philosophy: One omakase, built around what came in that morning; 走り・旬・名残 across the course.
chef_bio.specialty: 天麩羅会席【蝶尾】¥7,800 (13 items); 天麩羅と鮨会席【江戸錦】¥9,800 (18 items); 【和唐内】¥12,000 (16 items); 鮨と天麩羅会席【蘭鋳】¥15,000.

anecdotes.text: Every course is named after a variety of goldfish — 蝶尾 (butterfly-tail), 江戸錦, 和唐内, 蘭鋳 (ranchu) — the only visible flourish on an otherwise sober menu.
Tabelog reviewers describe it as a basement hideaway ten minutes on foot from Ginza where last orders run to 21:30, and note the private rooms can be had at short notice for a business lunch.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: The shop's own Gurunavi-hosted site gives 〒104-0031 東京都中央区京橋1-6-12 京橋イーサスビルB1, tel 03-6271-0062, lunch 11:30–15:00 (L.O.13:30) and dinner 17:00–23:30 (L.O.21:30), 定休日なし（不定休日あり）, 24 seats, all non-smoking, free Wi-Fi, お子様連れNG, cards accepted, and its embedded geodata 35.677456/139.772010. Tabelog (13290547) agrees on the address and phone, adds オープン日 2023年11月, the 10% service charge and the ¥8,000–9,999 dinner / ¥4,000–4,999 lunch bands. Ikyu carries the same address and phone.

gf_cross_contamination.text: Tempura is fried at the counter as part of every course; wheat batter and the fryer are central to the operation, not incidental.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Edomae nigiri brushed with nikiri (wheat soy sauce), plus dashi-seasoned wan and nimono courses; no tamari is mentioned anywhere.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Fish-led omakase with bonito dashi; no vegetarian course exists and there is no à la carte.

cultural_comfort.note: A quiet, formal basement counter aimed at business entertaining, anniversaries and dates — the room is hushed, cards are taken, the whole place is non-smoking and there is free Wi-Fi. Two things to know before booking: children are explicitly not admitted (お子様連れNG), and a 10% service charge is added. Parties of 7–10 wanting the private room are told to phone rather than book online, and the phone line is Japanese. Because it is one fixed omakase, any dietary change has to be agreed at the reservation, not at the counter.

enrich_note: CONFIRMED. Nationwide Yahoo Japan search on the full name returned Tabelog, Ikyu, Gurunavi/gorp, Hot Pepper and OpenRice listings that all agree on 東京都中央区京橋1-6-12 イーサスビルB1F and 03-6271-0062. Coordinates 35.677458/139.771933 are Tabelog's embedded geodata; the shop's own site independently gives 35.677456/139.772010, i.e. the same doorway. Opened November 2023, which is why the sweep had nothing on it.

name: 天麩羅 えびのや 八重洲地下街店
closed_since: Marked 【閉店】 on Tabelog; the last of its 78 reviews is dated March 2024, and the branch is absent from Yaechika's current restaurant directory (checked 2026-08-20)
address_ja: 東京都中央区八重洲2-1 八重洲地下街（東エリア）— 閉店
cuisine: Was a 22-seat counter tempura stand in the Yaesu underground mall — tendon and tempura teishoku fried to order in fresh soybean oil, lunch tendon around ¥800 and a ¥500 tendon bentō, under ¥999 at lunch. Now closed.
neighborhood: Yaesu 2-1, east zone of Yaechika (the Yaesu underground mall) — 3–4 min from Tokyo Station's Yaesu underground central gate, 2–3 min from Nihombashi Station's Takashimaya exit, 350 m from Kyōbashi Station
hours_raw: （閉店時点）[月〜金] 11:00〜15:00 ／ 17:30〜21:00　定休日：土・日・祝（Retty）。An Instagram post at the April 2021 relaunch gave 10:00〜22:00, following the mall's hours.
gf_detail: Moot — the shop is closed. While it was open it was a dedicated tempura fryer: wheat batter, a shared fryer, tendon tare built on wheat soy sauce. No gluten-free claim was ever made by the brand.
vegan_detail: Moot — the shop is closed. The menu was prawn, squid, egg and mixed-vegetable tempura over rice with a soy-mirin tare; nothing vegan was offered.

roles: chain brand operated by 株式会社フジオフードシステム (Fujio Food System)
chef_bio.origin: Osaka — Fujio Food System, the group behind まいどおおきに食堂
chef_bio.background: Tenpura Ebinoya was not an owner-chef restaurant but one of Fujio Food System's brands: a counter format where the tempura is fried to order in front of you in fresh soybean oil (新鮮な大豆白絞油) and served as a teishoku or a tendon at canteen prices. The Yaechika branch reopened after a refit in the east zone of the Yaesu underground mall in April 2021, and Yaechika's own account promoted its ¥500 tendon bentō that June. Tabelog reviewers through 2023–24 describe a fast-food tempura counter running a lunch-only tendon board at ¥800 with red-miso soup for ¥100. Tabelog now carries the page as 【閉店】, the last review is March 2024, and it does not appear in Yaechika's current restaurant listing. A separate えびのや 八重洲店 nearby is marked closed as well.
chef_bio.specialty: Lunch tendon ¥800; ¥500 tendon bentō; prawn, squid, green bean, aubergine, pumpkin and soft-boiled egg tempura.
chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Tabelog 13257971 heads the page 【閉店】天麩羅 えびのや 八重洲地下街店 and gives 東京都中央区八重洲2-1 八重洲地下街, 22 seats, all non-smoking, price band ～￥999, with reviews ending March 2024. A second Tabelog page (13225226) marks えびのや 八重洲店 closed too. Yaechika's own shop directory, filtered to レストラン・カフェ and read in full on 2026-08-20, lists no えびのや. Fujio Food System is the operator of record; its /brand/ebinoya/ URL now 404s.

cultural_comfort.note: Do not send anyone here. The unit in the east zone of Yaechika is gone; Yaechika's current directory contains no Ebinoya, and the nearby えびのや 八重洲店 is closed too. If someone wants cheap fried-to-order tempura in the same underground mall, てんや is still listed there.

enrich_note: CLOSED PERMANENTLY. The name in the light record is correct and the business was real, but it is shut. Yahoo Japan search on 「天麩羅 えびのや 八重洲地下街店」 and again on 「えびのや 八重洲地下街 閉店」 both surfaced the Tabelog page headed 【閉店】; the page was opened directly and confirms it, with the last of 78 reviews dated March 2024. Yaechika's own restaurant directory was then fetched and read in full — roughly 90 tenants, alphabetical あ行 to わ行 — and contains no えびのや. A second Tabelog page shows the sister branch えびのや 八重洲店 is closed as well. Coordinates set to Tabelog's embedded geodata for the unit so the record is at least accurate about where it used to be; recommend hiding the record.

name: 京料理と創作和食 刻（KIZAMI）
address_ja: 〒104-0031 東京都中央区京橋1-5-1 5F（旧所在地：東京都中央区八重洲2-5-7 三興ビル1F）
cuisine: Private-room banquet izakaya billing itself as Kyoto cooking and creative washoku — the published draw is the party plan at ¥4,400 for a course with two hours of all-you-can-drink, average spend about ¥4,000; the 12:00–16:00 slot is reservation-only
neighborhood: Kyōbashi 1-chōme — 1 min from Kyōbashi Station (Ginza line), about 217 m; also walkable from Tokyo Station's Yaesu side
hours_raw: 12:00～24:00（12:00〜16:00はご予約のみ承っております。直接ご連絡ください。）／旧店舗表記では年中無休
gf_detail: Nothing published on gluten. It is a banquet izakaya running set courses with unlimited drinks, and no menu detail survives online beyond the price points, so the only honest answer is that a celiac would have to phone ahead in Japanese. Treat the default assumptions as applying: wheat shōyu in every sauce, a shared fryer for the karaage-and-tempura end of an izakaya board, and course menus fixed in advance. Do not rely on this record — see the note about whether the shop is still trading.
vegan_detail: No vegetarian or vegan information is published anywhere, and the surviving menu material is only course prices. A banquet izakaya course will normally be fish- and meat-led with dashi throughout. Ask before booking.

chef_bio.background: Kizami traded as 京料理と創作和食 刻 八重洲店 at 東京都中央区八重洲2-5-7 三興ビル 1F — 40 seats, private rooms for 2 up to 30-plus, bookable out for 20–50, and, unusually for the area, smoking permitted throughout. Tabelog has since re-flagged that page 【移転】 and points to a successor listing simply called 刻 (KIZAMI) at 東京都中央区京橋1-5-1 5F, phone 03-4540-1042, with no reviews yet. Gurunavi carries the shop under the old trading name but at the new Kyōbashi address, with 12:00–24:00 hours (12:00–16:00 by reservation only), 40 seats, English and both simplified and traditional Chinese menus, and English- and Chinese-speaking staff. Its own gorp-hosted official site now returns an empty page. No named chef appears in any source, and the 'Kyoto cuisine' billing is not backed by any published dish list.
chef_bio.specialty: Banquet course with 2 hours of all-you-can-drink from ¥4,400.
chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Tabelog 13265694 is headed 【移転】京料理と創作和食 刻 八重洲店 and gives the former address 八重洲2-5-7 三興ビル1F with 40 seats and 12:00–24:00 / 年中無休. Tabelog 13293005 is the successor page, 刻 (KIZAMI), 東京都中央区京橋1-5-1 5F, 03-4540-1042, zero reviews, explicitly noting ※このお店は以前の場所から移転しています. Gurunavi 24a6uyra0000 gives 〒104-0031 東京都中央区京橋1-5-1 5F, 03-4540-1042, 12:00～24:00 with the 12:00–16:00 reservation-only caveat, 40 seats, foreign-language menus and staff. OpenRice lists it with 03-4590-0011 and the official URL https://ghjw609.gorp.jp/, which now returns an empty JSON shell — the shop page has been taken down.

positives.text: Gurunavi records English and Chinese menus and English- and Chinese-speaking staff, which at least makes a dietary conversation possible if the shop is still trading.

cultural_comfort.note: On paper this is an easy room for a foreign visitor — private rooms from two people, English and Chinese menus, staff who speak both, and a flat all-in banquet price. Two caveats. The old Yaesu premises were 全席喫煙可, smoking throughout, and nothing published says the new floor is different. And the daytime slot is reservation-only by phone. Before going out of your way, phone 03-4540-1042 and confirm the shop is open at all — see the enrich note.

enrich_note: PROBABLE — real business, current operation unconfirmed. The name in the light record is correct, but the shop has moved: Tabelog flags 京料理と創作和食 刻 八重洲店 (八重洲2-5-7 三興ビル1F) as 【移転】 and links a successor page, 刻 (KIZAMI), at 京橋1-5-1 5F; Gurunavi carries the old trading name at the new address with live hours and a working phone. Against that, the successor Tabelog page has zero reviews, and the shop's own official site (ghjw609.gorp.jp) now serves an empty page. Coordinates moved to the new Kyōbashi address using Tabelog's embedded geodata. DUPLICATE WARNING for the merge: 京橋1-5-1 is the same address as two other records in this shard, tokyo3_ky_63 (肉の蔵 八重洲日本橋店) and tokyo3_tokyo_ky (お箸とグラス TOKYO 八重洲日本橋店), which share coordinates with this one and are almost certainly the same 80-seat operation under different brand names — a Hot Pepper reviewer says as much in as many words. Searches run: Yahoo Japan on 「京料理と創作和食 刻 八重洲店」 and again on 「刻 KIZAMI 京橋1-5-1 居酒屋」; both Tabelog pages and the Gurunavi page fetched and read; the official gorp site fetched (HTTP 200, empty payload); Hot Pepper keyword search 404'd and Retty returned HTTP 406.

name: 黄金出汁鍋と厳選肉料理 居酒屋 肉の蔵 八重洲日本橋店
cuisine: Eighty-seat private-room banquet izakaya built on hotpot and meat — Hakata-style mizutaki from a six-hour chicken-bone broth, Hakata motsunabe (¥1,280 a portion, minimum two), pork shabu, morning-killed chicken grilled over charcoal, and sashimi trucked in daily from Toyosu; course plans with two hours of free drinks run ¥4,400–6,600, à la carte spend around ¥5,000 plus a 10% service charge
neighborhood: Kyōbashi 1-chōme — about 2 min from Nihombashi Station (Ginza / Tozai / Toei Asakusa lines), 3 min from Kyōbashi Station exit 7, and a short walk from Tokyo Station's Yaesu side
hours_raw: 月～日、祝日、祝前日 11:00～翌0:00（料理L.O. 23:00／ドリンクL.O. 23:00）※11:00～16:00は予約のみ承ります／定休日：不定休日あり
gf_detail: No gluten-free claim and no allergen page. Two things on this menu are worth a conversation rather than an outright no: the house mizutaki is described as built from chicken bones alone, 他の調味料を一切使わずに — no other seasoning at all — thirty carcasses simmered six hours, so the broth itself should be wheat-free, and the yakitori can be ordered shio rather than tare. Everything around them is not: the ponzu you dip mizutaki in is wheat shōyu, the mizutaki finishes with 極太ちゃんぽん麺 (thick wheat noodles), motsunabe sits on a soy-and-miso base, and an 80-seat banquet kitchen with karaage, gyōza and fried plates has a shared fryer. There is no evidence the staff are trained on cross-contact. Phone ahead in Japanese; do not walk in and improvise.
vegan_detail: A meat-and-hotpot izakaya: chicken, pork shabu, offal, horse sashimi, Toyosu fish. Nothing vegan is offered as a dish, and the set courses are all animal-led. What is realistically available is the standard izakaya edge — salads, edamame, chips, pickles — and even those are likely dressed with dashi or wheat shōyu. Note also that an お通し (cover charge appetiser) is served automatically and you do not choose it.

roles: multi-brand izakaya operation; no chef or company named in public listings
chef_bio.background: Niku no Kura is one of at least three izakaya brands trading out of the same address at 京橋1-5-1, a couple of minutes from Nihombashi Station — the others being お箸とグラス -TOKYO- 八重洲日本橋店 and, on the fifth floor, 刻 (KIZAMI). All three carry the same 80-seat/60-guest banquet capacity, the same 11:00–24:00 hours with a reservation-only daytime, the same 10% service charge and ¥500 Friday seat charge, and consecutive phone numbers in the 03-4588-17xx block; a Hot Pepper reviewer of the sister brand states flatly that they are 'the same sort of place with only the name different'. The published identity is banquet-first: fully enclosed tatami-style private rooms from two people up to a 60-person buy-out, tablet ordering, free Wi-Fi, an English menu, step-free access and children welcome. The cooking it advertises is Hakata hotpot — mizutaki from a chicken-bone-only stock, motsunabe — alongside charcoal yakitori from morning-killed birds and daily Toyosu fish. No chef is named and no operating company is named on any listing.
chef_bio.philosophy: Banquet izakaya: private rooms, a flat course price and two hours of free drinks.
chef_bio.specialty: 自家製コラーゲンたっぷり水炊き鍋 finished with thick chanpon noodles; 博多もつ鍋 ¥1,280; 肉の蔵豚しゃぶコース ¥4,500 with 2h free drinks; charcoal yakitori.

anecdotes.text: The mizutaki is advertised as thirty chicken carcasses simmered six hours with no other seasoning at all — the one dish here whose base is plausibly wheat-free.
Reviews are few and mixed: five stars from an after-party in December 2025 for the range of snacks and drinks, and a one-star in April 2026 from a guest whose booking was cancelled at the door.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Hot Pepper strJ004470695 (updated 2026-03-06) gives 東京都中央区京橋1-5-1, 11:00–24:00 with L.O. 23:00 and a reservation-only 11:00–16:00, 不定休日あり, 80 seats / 60 max banquet, private rooms from two, Wi-Fi, barrier-free, English menu, children welcome, VISA/Master and PayPay/Alipay, a 10% service charge and a ¥500 seat charge on Fridays and holiday eves, plus the full dish and course list. Tabelog 13316911 confirms 東京都中央区京橋1-5-1 and phone 03-4588-1738 with embedded geodata 35.678565/139.769790. Jalan gives the same hours and 東京メトロ日本橋駅より徒歩約2分; Yahoo Map gives 京橋駅出口7から徒歩約3分; Retty lists 03-4588-1733.

gf_cross_contamination.text: An 80-seat banquet kitchen running fried izakaya plates and finishing its hotpots with wheat chanpon noodles in the same pots guests eat from. No wheat-free handling is claimed.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Ordinary wheat shōyu assumed: ponzu for the mizutaki, tare for the yakitori, the motsunabe base and the sashimi soy. No tamari is mentioned.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Chicken, pork, offal, horse and fish across the whole board, with shared hotpots and a compulsory unchosen お通し.

positives.text: The mizutaki broth is advertised as chicken bones and nothing else — no seasoning added — which is a genuinely unusual starting point if you can then keep wheat soy sauce out of the bowl.
English menu, tablet ordering and fully enclosed private rooms make it easier than most banquet izakaya to have a slow, specific conversation about what is in a dish.

cultural_comfort.note: Straightforward for a foreign visitor: an English menu, tablet ordering, Wi-Fi, cards and PayPay/Alipay, step-free access, private rooms from two people and children welcome. Book — the 11:00–16:00 daytime slot takes reservations only, and one reviewer was turned away at the door when a booking went astray, so reconfirm. Two costs that are easy to miss: a 10% service charge at settlement and a ¥500 seat charge on Fridays and the eves of public holidays, plus the usual unchosen お通し. Smoking is 分煙 without a partition, so ask for a non-smoking private room if that matters.

name: 東北うまいもん居酒屋 地鶏×旬菜 お箸とグラス -TOKYO- 八重洲日本橋店
cuisine: Eighty-seat all-private-room banquet izakaya trading on Tōhoku produce and jidori chicken — Toyosu fish delivered every morning, beef sukiyaki hotpot, a five-piece sashimi assortment, Kumamoto horse sashimi, Hakata motsunabe ¥1,280, karashi-mentaiko cooked however you ask; course plans with two hours of free drinks from about ¥4,000, à la carte around ¥5,000 plus a 10% service charge
neighborhood: Kyōbashi 1-chōme — about 2 min from Nihombashi Station (Ginza / Tozai / Toei Asakusa lines), a short walk from Tokyo Station's Yaesu side and from Kyōbashi Station
hours_raw: 月～日、祝日、祝前日 11:00～翌0:00（料理L.O. 23:00／ドリンクL.O. 23:00）※11:00～16:00は予約のみ承ります／定休日：不定休日あり
gf_detail: No gluten-free claim and no allergen information. The board is a standard banquet izakaya one and wheat is everywhere it usually is: sashimi soy and ponzu are wheat shōyu, the sukiyaki warishita is soy-and-mirin, the motsunabe base is soy and miso (and 麦味噌, barley miso, is common in that dish and is not ruled out here), and karaage and other fried plates share a fryer. Raw fish, horse sashimi and grilled jidori ordered shio are the naturally wheat-free corners, but the dipping sauce arrives as standard and there is no evidence staff are trained to hold it. Phone ahead in Japanese if it matters.
vegan_detail: Chicken, beef, horse, offal and Toyosu fish across the entire published menu; every course plan is animal-led and there is no vegetarian option. The realistic vegan order is salads, edamame and pickles — and even those will likely carry dashi or wheat shōyu. An unchosen お通し cover dish is served automatically.

roles: multi-brand izakaya operation; no chef or company named in public listings
chef_bio.background: Ohashi to Glass -TOKYO- presents itself as a Tōhoku-produce izakaya built on jidori chicken and seasonal vegetables, with fully enclosed shōji-screened private rooms from two people up to a 60-guest buy-out, fish delivered from Toyosu every morning, tablet ordering and free Wi-Fi. In practice it is one of at least three brands trading from the same 80-seat premises at 京橋1-5-1 — the others being 肉の蔵 八重洲日本橋店 and, on the fifth floor, 刻 (KIZAMI) — sharing the same capacity, the same 11:00–24:00 hours with a reservation-only daytime, the same 10% service charge and ¥500 Friday seat charge, and phone numbers a few digits apart in the 03-4588-17xx block. One Hot Pepper reviewer, in for a Sunday lunchtime drink in May 2026, wrote that beyond salted tongue there was nothing recognisably Tōhoku on the table and that it was 'the same sort of place with only the name different'. Reviews average 2.3 out of 5 across six entries, with complaints about brusque service and small portions for the price. No chef and no operating company is named anywhere.
chef_bio.philosophy: Banquet izakaya: enclosed private rooms, a flat course price and two hours of free drinks.
chef_bio.specialty: 牛すき焼き鍋 and a five-piece sashimi assortment in the ¥-set 美味コース (10 items, 2h free drinks); 博多もつ鍋 ¥1,280 (min. two portions); 熊本県産馬刺し; 辛子明太子 served raw or lightly seared to order.

anecdotes.text: The house rule is no under-20s at all, including accompanied minors — unusual for an izakaya that elsewhere advertises itself as welcoming children in the private rooms, and the two claims sit side by side on the same listing.
A May 2026 reviewer who came for a Sunday lunchtime drink found the room empty but for his party and reported that apart from salted tongue nothing on the table was actually from Tōhoku.

gf_cross_contamination.text: An 80-seat banquet kitchen with fried plates and shared hotpots; no wheat-free handling is claimed anywhere.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Wheat shōyu assumed throughout — sashimi soy, sukiyaki warishita, motsunabe base. No tamari is mentioned. Barley miso is common in Hakata motsunabe and is not ruled out here.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Chicken, beef, horse, offal and daily Toyosu fish across the whole menu, plus a compulsory unchosen お通し.

positives.text: Enclosed private rooms from two people, an English menu and tablet ordering make a careful, unhurried order easier than at an open izakaya counter.

cultural_comfort.note: Physically easy — English menu, tablet ordering, Wi-Fi, cards and PayPay/Alipay, step-free access, and shōji-screened private rooms from two people. Three things to know. No one under 20 is admitted, even accompanied. A 10% service charge is added at settlement and a ¥500 seat charge applies on Fridays and holiday eves, on top of the unchosen お通し. And the reviews are poor — 2.3 out of 5, with repeated complaints about curt service and small portions for the money — so go for the private room and the drinks plan rather than the cooking. Smoking is 分煙 with no partition; ask for a non-smoking room.
